SILAC-Based Proteomic Source Attribution and EV-PC Protein Classification

Xueli Xu

2026-10-23

1 Overview

This report reproduces the full Heavy/Light isotope-based serum-source analysis using the serumsource R package. The entire computation runs in one line, and all downstream outputs (plots, tables, report) run in one more line.

The core question per protein: is this EV protein really carried by serum, or is it just background / residual EV material?

2 The whole analysis in two lines

library(serumsource)

# 1. Core computation (no I/O) -- one call
core <- run_core_analysis(input_file = "F:/WYF/NP_1/MaxQuant_annotated_with_total.xlsx")

# 2. Downstream: plots + CSV/XLSX + Markdown report -- one call
source("downstream/downstream_analysis.R")
run_downstream_analysis(core_result = core,
                        input_file  = "F:/WYF/NP_1/MaxQuant_annotated_with_total.xlsx",
                        output_dir  = "output")

Everything below is the result of these two lines.

3 Configuration

All arguments have sensible defaults for the NP_1 dataset. Here we make them explicit for clarity:

library(serumsource)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))
library(knitr)

input_file      <- "F:/WYF/NP_1/MaxQuant_annotated_with_total.xlsx"
sheet_name      <- 1
sample_info     <- build_sample_info()
reference_group <- "UCEV"
target_groups   <- NULL          # auto = all groups except UCEV
params          <- serum_source_params()
output_dir      <- "F:/WYF/NP_1/提交/full_analysis_report/output"
dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Thresholds (defaults)
data.frame(Parameter = names(params), Value = as.character(unlist(params))) %>%
  kable(caption = "Threshold parameters (serum_source_params defaults)")
Threshold parameters (serum_source_params defaults)
Parameter Value
min_valid_reps 2
min_absolute_light_excess 0.05
background_multiplier_high 3
background_multiplier_medium 2
min_support_reps_when_three_valid 2
min_support_reps_when_two_valid 2
max_serum_fraction_cv_high_confidence 0.5
minimum_fraction_sd_floor 0.02
min_light_dominance_ratio 0.7
eps 1e-12

4 Run Core Analysis

One call reads the workbook, builds the long table, estimates the UCEV background, classifies every target group and performs source correction.

core <- run_core_analysis(
  input_file      = input_file,
  sheet_name      = sheet_name,
  sample_info     = sample_info,
  reference_group = reference_group,
  target_groups   = target_groups,
  params          = params
)

cat("Proteins:        ", nrow(core$annotation), "\n")
## Proteins:         5298
cat("Comparisons:     ", length(unique(core$results$comparison)), "\n")
## Comparisons:      4
cat("Global SD floor: ", round(core$global_fraction_sd_floor, 4), "\n")
## Global SD floor:  0.02

Returned list elements:

data.frame(Element = names(core)) %>%
  kable(caption = "List elements returned by run_core_analysis()")
List elements returned by run_core_analysis()
Element
lh_long
annotation
data_converted
ucev_sd
global_fraction_sd_floor
results
all_merged
primary_serum
case_summary
database_summary

Now load the downstream script for plotting helpers (used below):

source("F:/WYF/NP_1/提交/SerumSourceAnalyzer/downstream/downstream_analysis.R")

10 Calibrated Serum Light Intensity

all_merged adds Serum_L_Calibrated_<sample> columns, converting each replicate’s excess into calibrated serum Light intensity units.

cal_cols <- grep("^Serum_L_Calibrated", names(core$all_merged), value = TRUE)
cat("Calibrated columns added:", length(cal_cols), "\n")
## Calibrated columns added: 12
core$all_merged %>%
  select(Protein_Row_ID, Gene_names, all_of(cal_cols[1:min(4, length(cal_cols))])) %>%
  head(10) %>%
  kable(caption = "Preview of calibrated serum Light intensity (first 4 samples)")

11 Save Outputs

One call writes all CSV tables, the XLSX workbook and the Markdown report.

run_downstream_analysis(
  core_result     = core,
  input_file      = input_file,
  output_dir      = output_dir,
  sample_info     = sample_info,
  reference_group = reference_group,
  target_groups   = target_groups,
  params          = params,
  make_plots      = FALSE,
  save_outputs    = TRUE,
  write_report    = FALSE,
  render_notebook = FALSE
)

cat("Output files (", length(list.files(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)), "):\n", sep = "")
## Output files (48):
print(list.files(output_dir, recursive = TRUE))
